messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Estimate the standard error of ESW in R
parts:
Jeferson

The Distance package in R does not produce an estimate of SE(ESW). However, with a small amount of hand calculation you can produce it.  Recognise that CV(ESW) = CV(P_a) and further note SE(ESW) = CV(ESW) x ESW.

Hence from the reported CV(P_a) coupled with the estimate of ESW you can produce by multiplying the truncation distance (w) by P_a, the quantity you desire can be produced.

Calculation from the old "duck nest" data set:

P_a = 0.86711
w = 8
CV(P_a) = 0.0454

results in
ESW = 8 * 0.86711 = 6.9369
SE(ESW) = CV(ESW) * ESW = 0.0454 * 6.9369 = 0.3149
